t0.said: Hold still: P I D control, flown on a rocket.

t1.said: This is a hopper: a test rocket with one engine. Its job is to lift off, and hold still at a set height.

t2.said: The engine can only push along the rocket. A computer sets the throttle many times a second, and the engine always answers a moment late.

p1.said: Idea one: the further below the target, the harder it pushes. That is P, for proportional.

p2.said: It shoots past, falls back, and every swing is bigger than the last. The engine answers late, so every push arrives late.

p3.said: Until it slams into the pad.

d1.said: Idea two: also push against the speed. Climbing fast? Ease off. Falling? Push harder. That is D, for derivative.

d2.said: No more swinging. But it settles below the target.

d3.said: To hover, the engine must carry the weight, and P only pushes that hard when the rocket is below the target. So the gap never closes.

i1.said: Idea three: add up the error over time, and push with that sum too. That is I, for integral.

i2.said: While any gap is left, the sum keeps growing, until the rocket sits right on the target, and stays there.

w1.said: One catch. On the climb the gap is large for seconds, and the sum piles up. So this rocket shoots far past the target.

w2.said: The fix: stop adding while the engine is already at full throttle. Now it barely overshoots.

g1.said: Two more loops keep it upright by swinging the engine. A gust shoves the rocket sideways; it leans into it, and flies back over the pad.

l1.said: To land, move the target down a little every step, and let the same three terms follow it.

l2.said: The engine cuts at touchdown, and the rocket settles softly on its legs.
